## 05 · Audit & verify
After the loop, SQL compares this run with the last `COMPLETE` run of the **same scope** and writes changes. `Verify audit` checks the BigQuery response.

**Validate in BigQuery:**
- `scan_runs`: latest run has `status = COMPLETE`
- `resources`: count rows for that `run_id`
- `changes`: review differences after a second run

**Before production:** repeat with no changes, test a controlled addition/removal, and test failure handling. BigQuery streaming visibility and volatile metadata can affect comparisons.

## 04 · Persist inventory
`Batch loop` writes each batch to BigQuery `resources` via `tabledata.insertAll`. `Verify inserted batch` rejects reported insert errors.

**Credential:** Google Service Account API; enable **Set up for use in HTTP Request node** and set OAuth scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.

All HTTP Request nodes must use the same authorized credential.

## 03 · Asset discovery
Enable **Cloud Asset API**. Grant **Cloud Asset Viewer** on the chosen scope; access to other projects is not automatic.

`Search Cloud Assets` calls `searchAllResources`. Pagination passes `nextPageToken` as query `pageToken` and stops when no token remains. `Normalize & batch` prepares batches of up to 250 rows.

Coverage depends on supported asset types and IAM visibility.

## 02 · BigQuery setup
Enable **BigQuery API**. Pre-create the dataset or grant temporary dataset-creation rights. These nodes create/check `cloud_inventory` and its tables: `resources`, `scan_runs`, `changes`.

**IAM:** BigQuery Job User on the execution project; dataset-scoped Data Editor for writing. Avoid project-wide BigQuery Admin. Dataset creation needs additional project-level permission.

## 01 · Run & scope
**Daily schedule:** 03:15 in the workflow timezone; or use **Manual start**.

In **Configuration**, set `scope`, `billingProject`, `dataset`, and `location` (`EU` by default). Example scope: `projects/PROJECT_ID`. `Initialize run` assigns a unique run ID.

**Start with a small project.** Schedule only after validation.

# Google Cloud Inventory & Change Audit

**Automated Google Cloud asset discovery, inventory snapshots, and change detection with n8n and BigQuery.**

This workflow automatically discovers Google Cloud projects accessible to a Service Account, collects resource metadata using **Cloud Asset Inventory**, and stores historical snapshots in **BigQuery**. It compares consecutive completed scans to identify resources that have been **added, modified, or removed**.

## How it works

1. **Discover** — Automatically find accessible Google Cloud organizations, folders, and projects.
2. **Inventory** — Collect supported cloud resources using Cloud Asset Inventory API with pagination.
3. **Store** — Normalize resource metadata and persist historical snapshots in BigQuery.
4. **Audit** — Compare each snapshot against the previous completed scan to detect `ADDED`, `MODIFIED`, and `REMOVED` resources.
5. **Validate** — Verify snapshot integrity and prevent incomplete scans from being marked as complete.

Runs manually or automatically using a configurable daily schedule.

## Setup

1. **Google Cloud** — Enable Cloud Resource Manager, Cloud Asset Inventory, and BigQuery APIs.
2. **Service Account** — Create a dedicated Service Account with `Browser`, `Cloud Asset Viewer`, `BigQuery Job User`, and `BigQuery Data Editor` roles, assigned at the appropriate scopes.
3. **n8n Credentials** — Configure a **Google Service Account API** credential with HTTP Request support and the `cloud-platform` OAuth scope. Assign it to all HTTP Request nodes.
4. **Configuration** — Set `inventoryProjectId` to the Google Cloud project hosting BigQuery. Other settings have defaults.
5. **Run & Validate** — Execute manually, verify the BigQuery results, then activate the schedule.

**No custom IAM roles or manual target-project lists required.** Discovery is based on the Service Account's effective permissions.

## Output & limitations

- **BigQuery tables:** `resources`, `scan_runs`, `changes`.
- **Safety:** Transactional snapshots, integrity checks, pagination validation, and failure-safe completion.
- **Limit:** 5 MiB normalized resource payload per project.
- **Coverage:** IAM permissions and Cloud Asset Inventory-supported resource types determine visibility.

Errors stop execution rather than silently completing partial scans. Configure an n8n Error Workflow for notifications.

**[Full documentation, setup guide & SQL queries → Notion](https://www.notion.so/402f0ba27c32801ba303f2549dbe9fa2)**

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ (() => { const cfg = $('Initialize run').first().json; return JSON.stringify({query:`DECLARE current_run STRING DEFAULT '${cfg.runId}'; DECLARE current_scope STRING DEFAULT '${cfg.scope}'; DECLARE previous_run STRING; SET previous_run=(SELECT run_id FROM \`${cfg.billingProject}.${cfg.dataset}.scan_runs\` WHERE scope=current_scope AND status='COMPLETE' ORDER BY finished_at DESC LIMIT 1); INSERT INTO \`${cfg.billingProject}.${cfg.dataset}.changes\` (run_id,scope,asset_name,change_type,detected_at) WITH cur AS (SELECT asset_name,metadata_json FROM \`${cfg.billingProject}.${cfg.dataset}.resources\` WHERE run_id=current_run), prev AS (SELECT asset_name,metadata_json FROM \`${cfg.billingProject}.${cfg.dataset}.resources\` WHERE run_id=previous_run) SELECT current_run,current_scope,COALESCE(c.asset_name,p.asset_name),CASE WHEN p.asset_name IS NULL THEN 'ADDED' WHEN c.asset_name IS NULL THEN 'REMOVED' ELSE 'MODIFIED' END,CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() FROM cur c FULL OUTER JOIN prev p USING(asset_name) WHERE previous_run IS NOT NULL AND (c.asset_name IS NULL OR p.asset_name IS NULL OR c.metadata_json!=p.metadata_json); INSERT INTO \`${cfg.billingProject}.${cfg.dataset}.scan_runs\` (run_id,scope,started_at,finished_at,status,asset_count) SELECT current_run,current_scope,TIMESTAMP('${cfg.startedAt}'),CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(),'COMPLETE',COUNT(*) FROM \`${cfg.billingProject}.${cfg.dataset}.resources\` WHERE run_id=current_run;`,useLegacySql:false,location:cfg.location,timeoutMs:200000}); })() }}

parameters.jsCode: const cfg=$('Initialize run').first().json;const pages=$input.all().map(x=>x.json);const assets=[];if(pages.length && pages[pages.length-1].nextPageToken) throw Error('Pagination incomplete: final page has nextPageToken');for(const p of pages){if(p.error) throw Error('Asset API error: '+JSON.stringify(p.error));for(const a of (p.results||[])){assets.push({insertId:cfg.runId+'|'+a.name,json:{run_id:cfg.runId,observed_at:cfg.startedAt,scope:cfg.scope,asset_name:a.name||'',asset_type:a.assetType||'',project:a.project||'',location:a.location||'',display_name:a.displayName||'',metadata_json:JSON.stringify(a)}})}}const batches=[];for(let i=0;i<assets.length;i+=250)batches.push({json:{...cfg,rows:assets.slice(i,i+250),batch:i/250}});if(!batches.length)batches.push({json:{...cfg,rows:[],batch:0}});return batches;
const r=$input.first().json;if(r.errors?.length||r.jobComplete===false) throw Error('BigQuery DDL failed/incomplete: '+JSON.stringify(r));return [{json:$('Initialize run').first().json}];

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({query:`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \`${$json.billingProject}.${$json.dataset}.resources\` (run_id STRING, observed_at TIMESTAMP, scope STRING, asset_name STRING, asset_type STRING, project STRING, location STRING, display_name STRING, metadata_json STRING) PARTITION BY DATE(observed_at) CLUSTER BY scope,asset_type; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \`${$json.billingProject}.${$json.dataset}.scan_runs\` (run_id STRING, scope STRING, started_at TIMESTAMP, finished_at TIMESTAMP, status STRING, asset_count INT64); CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS \`${$json.billingProject}.${$json.dataset}.changes\` (run_id STRING, scope STRING, asset_name STRING, change_type STRING, detected_at TIMESTAMP);`,useLegacySql:false,location:$json.location,timeoutMs:200000}) }}

parameters.jsCode: const r=$input.first().json; if(r.error && r.error.code!==409) throw Error('Dataset setup: '+JSON.stringify(r.error)); return [{json:$('Initialize run').first().json}];

const c=$input.first().json; if(!/^(projects|folders|organizations)\/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(c.scope)) throw Error('Invalid scope'); for(const k of ['billingProject','dataset']) if(!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(c[k])) throw Error('Invalid '+k); const runId=String(Date.now())+'-'+Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,10); return [{json:{...c,runId,startedAt:new Date().toISOString()}}];
